bibliographic.title: In situ study of zinc peroxide decomposition to zinc oxide by X-ray absorption spectroscopy and reverse Monte-Carlo simulations

affiliations.text: Institute of Solid State Physics, University of Latvia, Kengaraga street 8, LV-1063 Riga, Latvia
MAX IV Laboratory, Lund University, PO BOX 118, SE-22100 Lund, Sweden

bibliographic.abstract: The Zn K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy has been used to investigate in situ the decomposition of zinc peroxide (ZnO2) to zinc oxide (ZnO). Principal component and linear combination analyses of the EXAFS spectra have been employed to identify the phase composition of the oxide upon heating to 900 °C. Only the ZnO2 phase has been found up to 180 °C, whereas only the nanocrystalline ZnO phase has occurred above 250 °C. Detailed structural information on the temperature dependence of the local environment of zinc atoms has been obtained using the reverse Monte Carlo simulations. A strong increase of disorder has been found upon approaching the decomposition temperature, evidenced by the broadening of Zn–O and Zn–Zn pair distribution functions and related mean-square relative displacements.

samples.sample_description: Nanocrystalline zinc peroxide with crystallite size of about 22 nm.

datasets.dataset_description: In situ temperature-dependent Zn K-edge XANES and EXAFS spectra collected during the decomposition of ZnO2 to ZnO from 20 to 900 °C.

datasets.dataset_name: Principal component analysis of EXAFS spectra
datasets.dataset_description: PCA of Zn K-edge EXAFS spectra to determine phase composition during ZnO2 decomposition.

datasets.dataset_name: Linear combination analysis of EXAFS spectra
datasets.dataset_description: LCA of Zn K-edge EXAFS spectra to quantify phase fractions during ZnO2 decomposition.

datasets.dataset_name: Reverse Monte Carlo simulations of EXAFS spectra
datasets.dataset_description: RMC simulations of Zn K-edge EXAFS spectra to extract atomic pair distribution functions and bond angle distribution functions.
